## PURULENT SKIN/SOFT TISSUE INFECTIONS
Includes furuncles/boils, carbuncles and cutaneous abscesses with or without
surrounding inflammation. The predominant pathogen is Staphylococcus aureus
(MSSA or MRSA).
Incision and drainage are recommended whenever feasible. Adjunctive antibiotics
are typically recommended. Incision and drainage alone are reasonable based on
patient preferences when abscess is smaller, limited surrounding inflammation,
no systemic signs of infections, and/or limited comorbidities.
## For recurrent skin abscesses in addition to culture and antibiotic therapy
## recommend considering a decolonization regimen.
[[Click Here] for Staphylococcus aureus Decolonization](orzid2-gmenu-abx-staphylococcus-aureus-decolonization)
## Preferred oral therapy:
[Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet BID for 5 days [R,DI]](psjzid-trimeth-sulfa-1-ds-tab-bid)
< OR >
[Doxycycline 100 mg PO BID for 5 days [DI]](psjzid-doxycycline-100mg-po-q12h)
## Preferred IV therapy:
[Vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q 12 hours [R]](orz-set-abx-vanco-new-start-15mg-kg-q12h-mrsa-nares-screening)
## Alternative:
Reserve for contraindication, precaution, failure to preferred options, or for
patient where parenteral antibiotics would be otherwise be selected.
[Linezolid 600 mg PO BID for 5 days [DI,O]](psjzid-linezolid-600mg-po-q12h)
